# Zig

Zig makes small, fast modules (the summary is 95 KB: about 30 ms for its first call, which compiles it, and 1.2 ms for later ones) and needs nothing but Zig: WASI is one of its targets. Its standard library has JSON, so a module reads and writes JSON with no packages.

## Set up

```bash
brew install zig   # Zig 0.17
```

Zig's standard library changes between versions. The example is written for Zig 0.17, where I/O goes through `std.Io` and `main` takes `std.process.Init`.

## The module

[`example/summary/zig`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/zig/src/main.zig):

```zig
pub fn main(init: std.process.Init) !void {
    const io = init.io;
    const allocator = init.arena.allocator();
    var out_buf: [4096]u8 = undefined;
    var stdout = std.Io.File.stdout().writerStreaming(io, &out_buf);
    const out = &stdout.interface;

    const args = try init.minimal.args.toSlice(allocator);
    const function: []const u8 = if (args.len > 1) args[1] else "";
    if (std.mem.eql(u8, function, "--describe")) {
        try out.writeAll(@embedFile("manifest.json"));
        return out.flush();
    }
    if (!std.mem.eql(u8, function, "run")) fail(io, "no_such_function", function);

    var in_buf: [4096]u8 = undefined;
    var stdin = std.Io.File.stdin().readerStreaming(io, &in_buf);
    const input = try stdin.interface.allocRemaining(allocator, .unlimited);
    const post = std.json.parseFromSliceLeaky(Post, allocator, input, .{ .ignore_unknown_fields = true }) catch
        fail(io, "bad_input", "the input isn't a post");
    // ... the summary
    try std.json.Stringify.value(.{ .text = text.items, .words = words.items.len }, .{}, out);
    try out.flush();
}
```

Flush the writer before returning: output still in its buffer is lost when the program exits.

## Build

In [`build.zig`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/zig/build.zig), target WASI, make the manifest importable, and set the stack:

```zig
const target = b.standardTargetOptions(.{
    .default_target = .{ .os_tag = .wasi, .cpu_arch = .wasm32 },
});
// ...
mod.addAnonymousImport("manifest.json", .{ .root_source_file = b.path("manifest.json") });
const exe = b.addExecutable(.{ .name = "summary", .root_module = mod });
exe.stack_size = 1 << 20; // Zig's default stack is 16 MB: every call would start with 16 MB of memory
```

```bash
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall
cp zig-out/bin/summary.wasm pb_hooks/summary.pb.wasm
```

A Zig module never says it's Zig, so the manifest says `"language": "Zig"`.

## Call it

```js
const out = await $wasm.run.async("summary", { title: e.record.get("title"), body: e.record.get("body") })
```

## C libraries

Zig compiles C as well: add C files to the module with `mod.addCSourceFiles(...)` and link libc (`mod.link_libc = true`), and a Zig module can use a C library directly. For C alone, see [C and C++](/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/c).
